label: r2c2
name: circular stem, long horizon
hypothesis: Same as r1c2 but with gamma 0.99 and gae_lambda 0.95. With gamma 0.95, the +1 exact-build bonus is discounted to about 0.6 by the time it reaches early placements. That weakens credit for build order (fill under overhangs before covering them) and for finishing instead of stopping early. A longer horizon should raise exact builds and placements per episode. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.43, or if episodes still end early.
last_analysis: Lining up the rolled target with the build is what unlocks learning. The starting network and every trial without circular row mixing collapsed to choosing DONE at once. Seed 0 is the bottleneck. It scored exactly 0.0781 in four different trials, so it reliably settles into a policy that fills layer 0 only and then stops. That suggests stacking is hard to perceive, because the conjunction 'build filled at z-1 here and target missing at z four columns away' must be learned inside one wide row conv. The recipe changes (more samples, a longer horizon, more entropy, small-gain initialisation) moved the mean by no more than seed noise. r1c1, with the default 4 epochs, had the most balanced seeds (0.31 / 0.49). The full-row and full-column trunk failed (seed 0 chose DONE immediately). The per-layer stem helped seed 0 only with entropy 0.04, and seed 1 fell at the same time. Final round: test a factorised alignment layer under two recipes, plus r1c1 with a long horizon.
